caption: Dubbed The Newsboy, this Robin was purchased in 1929 by the Daily Gazette newspaper of McCook, Nebraska. It flew 600 km a day to deliver 5,000 newspapers to 40 towns across rural Nebraska and Kansas. Publisher Harry Strunk hired pilot Steve Tuttle to deliver the Gazette in the morning and (hopefully) defray costs by selling flying lessons in the afternoon. At each town, Tuttle would drop a bundle of newspapers out of a hole in the bottom of the fuselage. After sustaining damage in a tornado, the aircraft was eventually sold, repaired, and flown sporadically in the ensuing decades. Restored in the late 1960s, it has been on loan to The Museum of Flight since 1972.

Doug Champlin purchased the P-40 in 1972 and had it fully restored by Dick Martin at Carlsbad, CA in 1979. The chosen markings are those of Colonel Phil Colman of the Chinese-American Composite Wing. caption: The Stinson SR “Reliant” was a high-wing cabin monoplane introduced in 1933. It offered many appealing amenities: a large 4-place cabin, ruggedness, maintainability, reliability, and easy handling. The SR was especially popular among sportsmen, business executives, and bush pilots. This Reliant was built in 1933. Its operational history is unclear, though unverified sources indicate that it was flown as both a landplane and a seaplane. It was donated to The Museum of Flight in 1990 by owner Robert Richardson.

Wfs. 05Nov1945. Transferred to Stuttgart, AR, for display as War Memorial until 1953. Sold to Biegert brothers of Shickley, Nebraska, she was overhauled into flying condition and converted to an aerial sprayer and fire bomber. Featured in the movies The Thousand Plane Raid (1968), Tora! Tora! Tora! (1970), and Memphis Belle (1989). In 1998 and reg.
